brief.topic: Writing a PRD for an AI feature exactly like a normal PRD
brief.audience: PMs writing specs for AI features

coreInsight: A standard PRD template assumes the software does what it is told; an AI PRD needs four extra sections — failure modes, eval plan, data dependencies and a cost envelope — before anyone builds.

caption.opening: A normal PRD template quietly assumes the software does what it’s told. AI features don’t.
body:
Four sections to add to every AI PRD:
→ Failure modes: what a wrong answer looks like, and the fallback
→ Eval plan: the test set, the metric, the pass bar
→ Data: what it reads, who owns it, how fresh it must be
→ Cost envelope: maximum cost and latency per task
Write them before the build starts. A blank section is a question the team will answer by accident later.
